title: Reconstructing a Boolean list from its code
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, let $L$ be a natural number, and let $w$ be a Boolean list of length $L$. Suppose every position $j$ with $|\alpha|\le j<L$ contains false. Then encoding the function that assigns to each $i\in\alpha$ the entry of $w$ at the position of $i$ recovers $w$ exactly.
hypotheses_covered: For every $j$, if $|\alpha|\le j$ and $j<L$, then the entry of $w$ at position $j$ (defaulting to false beyond its length) is false
